objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of the Nucleus in reducing lead fracture rates in patients with high-impact or high-frequency cardiac motion
baseline: Historical lead fracture rate per 1000 device-years in patients with high-impact or high-frequency cardiac motion
procedure: Recruit 1000 patients with a history of high-impact or high-frequency cardiac motion
Randomly assign patients to either the Nucleus group or the control group
Implant the Nucleus in the assigned group and standard lead in the control group
Record lead fracture rates per 1000 device-years at regular intervals
expected_result: A 30% decrease in lead fracture rate per 1000 device-years within the first 5 years post-implantation
falsification_condition: No significant decrease in lead fracture rate per 1000 device-years within the first 2 years post-implantation, or a lead fracture rate exceeding 20% per 1000 device-years within the first 5 years post-implantation
sample_requirements: 1000 patients with a history of high-impact or high-frequency cardiac motion
safety_constraints: Ensure that the Nucleus does not cause any adverse effects on the patient's cardiac function or overall health
information_gain: The effectiveness of the Nucleus in reducing lead fracture rates in patients with high-impact or high-frequency cardiac motion, and the potential for long-term device reliability and patient safety
